# Understanding Cairns: A Summary

## Core Concept: The Pulse
A pulse is a growth event. When you pulse a cairn, it grows by two components:
1. A fixed amount called the stride
2. A bonus equal to how many complete strides fit into the current height

The key insight: you must recalculate the bonus fresh each time, because the height keeps changing.

## Repeated Pulses
When pulsing multiple times, each pulse builds on the new height from the previous pulse. You cannot use shortcuts or apply a fixed bonus repeatedly—the bonus changes as the height increases. Track through each pulse sequentially.

## Leaks: Height-Dependent Loss
A leak causes permanent loss after each pulse. The amount lost depends on the new height: for every N marks in the post-pulse height, you lose 1 mark. This is different from a fixed drain—it scales with height.

## Drains: Fixed Cycle Loss
A drain removes the same number of marks after every pulse, regardless of height. Over many cycles, this can slow or eventually stop growth, depending on whether the pulse adds more than the drain removes.

## Working Backwards (Origin Finding)
To find the starting height, reverse the process: test which previous heights would pulse to your current height. Work backwards through each pulse sequentially until you reach the origin.

## Merging Cairns
Two cairns combine into one using weighted shares (fractions summing to 1) plus a tether adjustment. The tether's contribution depends on the shorter cairn's height. The result is the sum of weighted components plus the tether effect.
